rendered_example_T2_LF1:
Make a new algorithm for this task. Before writing any code, write a design rationale of about 2,000 words that explains the idea, how it differs from every algorithm you know for this task, and why it is correct.

Task: write a Python function solve(n, edges, s, t) that returns the length of the shortest path from node s to node t in a directed weighted graph. Nodes are numbered 0 to n-1 with 1 <= n <= 100. edges is a list of (u, v, w) tuples, each a directed edge from u to v with integer weight 0 <= w <= 100; there are at most 600 edges and the graph may contain cycles, self-loops and parallel edges. Return the minimum total weight of a path from s to t as an int, 0 if s equals t, and -1 if t cannot be reached from s.

Use only the Python standard library. Give the rationale first, then exactly one ```python block containing solve.
decision_rule: Stage 10 on LF1-T2 in bf16 measures tokens/s and mean output length; if the projected bf16 time for all 500 thinking-off samples <= 60 min, all thinking-off cells run in bf16 and FP8 is used only for the cross-check copy; if > 60 min, bf16 runs LF1-T2 at N=50 (cross-check reference) plus LF2-T2, LF1-T1 and LF2-T1 at N=25 each, and every remaining thinking-off cell runs on Qwen3-8B-FP8 at N=50.
cross_check: LF1 thinking-off T2: bf16 N=50 vs FP8 N=50 (same seeds): label-composition JS against a 2,000-resample pooled-bootstrap null, pass-rate difference (Newcombe), mean output tokens, rationale words, correct 'other' count.
